title: Pallet Storage Racking System
description: Enclosed is a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for pallet storage racking system at the U.S Embassy Amman � Jordan. If you would like to submit a quotation, follow the instructions in Section 3 of the solicitation, complete the required portions of the attached document, and submit it to the email address shown on the Standard Form 1442 (Box 8) that follows this letter. Quotations are due by September 8th, 2026 at 16:30 PM (Amman Time GMT+3). Quotations MUST be submitted by email to AmmanRFQ@state.gov. Offers sent to any other address or addressed to specific individuals will NOT be considered. Offers MUST be in the following format to be considered acceptable: Email subject line to include [Company/Offeror Name] and RFQ 19J01026Q0016. Attach all documents to the e-mail (Microsoft Word or PDF). We will not accept offers that include links, unsolicited offers, or hard copies. All technical quotations must be on white paper without company logos, watermarks, letterhead or any information that identifies the company. Offers submitted after the deadline or to the incorrect email address will not be considered. In addition to the Technical Proposal, offers must include the following for the package to be considered complete: SF-1449 Section 1, Pricing Schedule. Section 4, Evaluation Factors (Additional information as required). Section 5, Representations and Certifications. Proof of Active SA M Registration Contract award The U.S. Government intends to award a contract to the responsible company submitting an acceptable offer at the lowest price. We intend to award a contract based on initial quotations, without holding discussions, although we may hold discussions with companies in the competitive range if there is a need to do so. The contractor shall attend a mandatory site visit where the pallet storage racking system will be explained, and any questions will be addressed. The site visit will be held at the U.S. Embassy on Monday August 31st, 2026, at 10:00 AM. Attendance is strongly encouraged. Offerors must register for the site visit by submitting the names of all attendees (Maximum 2 People) to ammanRFQquestions@state.gov no later than August 27th, 2026, at 4:00 PM local time. Offerors are required to submit all questions in writing to AmmanRFQquestions@state.gov by August 31st, 2026 at 4:30 PM local time. The questions and the Government's answers will be publicly available on the Embassy website. The U.S. Embassy is prohibited from procuring goods or services from any firms that are not registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). SAM is an integrated procurement database and serves as a single point of entry for vendors seeking to do business with the U.S. Government. If your company is selected to be awarded the contract, you will be required to complete the attached NDAA and Certification Regarding Compliance with Applicable Federal Anti-Discrimination Law.

title: VA OIG - CAFM Enterprise Support Services
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs, Office of Inspector General (VA OIG) has a requirement for OpenBlue brand software in a FedRAMP-Authorized cloud-based solution (Computer Aided Facility Management, CAFM) in accordance with the attached Statement of Work. VA OIG anticipates issuing a single, Firm Fixed Price (FFP) award in response to this RFQ. VA OIG anticipates making an award without negotiations. VA OIG does not anticipate a Question and Answers session for this requirement. Quotes shall be submitted by the deadline listed in this solicitation. Late submissions may not be considered for award. The anticipated Period of Performance will consist of a Base Period of 09/21/2026 - 09/20/2027, followed by four (4) Option Periods of twelve (12) months each. Quotes that do not price out Option Periods may not be considered for award. Quotes will be evaluated on a Lowest Price, Technically Acceptable (LPTA) basis. Price will be determined by adding all line items in submitted quotes across all Option Periods. Offerors are encouraged to provide any and all possible discounts. Offers will be ranked in terms of price. Should the lowest priced offer be evaluated as technically acceptable, no other offers will be evaluated and an award will be made to that offeror. Should the lowest priced offer be evaluated as technically unacceptable, the next lowest offer will be evaluated. Representations and Certifications: Certify the country of origin for each/product/service offered. Provide supplier and manufacturer data to support the certification. Maintain compliance documentation throughout the contract term. This acquisition is covered by the Trade Agreements Act (TAA). TAA compliance is required. Any proposed TAA compliant alternatives shall meet equivalent functional requirements. Applicable clauses are in the attached RFQ document. This is a Brand Name Only action. Please see the attached Brand Name Justification for details.

title: 26-58077 ACAN Integrated High‑Density Laser Diode Burn‑In and Characterization Platform
description: ACAN 26-58077 Integrated High-Density Laser Diode Burn-In and Characterization Platform 1. Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN) An ACAN is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that a department or agency intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date stated in the ACAN, the contracting officer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. 2. Definition of the Requirement The National Research Council of Canada (NRC), through the Canadian Photonics Fabrication Centre (CPFC), requires the supply, delivery, installation, commissioning, training, warranty, and support of an Integrated High-Density Laser Diode Burn-In and Characterization System (the "System"). The System must consist of a fully integrated high-density laser diode burn-in subsystem and a laser diode characterization subsystem operating within a common hardware, carrier, software, and data management architecture. The System will support reliability screening, accelerated life testing, and electro-optical characterization of compound semiconductor laser diode devices fabricated at CPFC, including edge-emitting distributed feedback (DFB) and Fabry-Perot (FP) laser diodes in chip-on-carrier form factors. The System must provide a fully integrated workflow that allows devices under test to remain mounted in a common carrier throughout burn-in and characterization processes without removal, remounting, repositioning, or re-alignment. The System must maintain consistent mechanical, electrical, thermal, and optical interfaces throughout testing while providing full traceability of device performance data. The requirement includes, but is not limited to: • Two (2) integrated burn-in racks; • Fourteen (14) burn-in drawers; • Fifty-six (56) burn-in fixtures; • Fifty-six (56) burn-in device carriers; • A minimum of 384 independent source-measure channels; • One (1) automated laser diode characterization system; • One (1) tri-temperature control subsystem supporting operation from approximately -5°C to 85°C; • Four (4) characterization carriers compatible with the common carrier architecture; • Integrated software for burn-in management, characterization, device tracking, automated test sequencing, and data management; • Engineering and customization services required to configure the System for NRC-CPFC devices; • Factory verification activities and associated documentation; • Shipping preparation, crating, vacuum sealing, and handling services; • Delivery, installation, commissioning, training, and Site Acceptance Testing; • Warranty support and technical support services. NRC will arrange any required field evaluation and site certification following installation. The Contractor shall provide the technical documentation and support necessary to facilitate the certification process. 3. Criteria for assessment of the Statement of Capabilities (Minimum Essential Requirements) Suppliers that consider themselves fully qualified and available to provide the goods and services described in this ACAN may submit a Statement of Capabilities demonstrating how their proposed System meets all of the following minimum essential requirements. A. Integrated System Architecture The proposed System must: • Consist of a high-density laser diode burn-in subsystem and a laser diode characterization subsystem supplied as a fully integrated solution; • Utilize a common carrier architecture between burn-in and characterization processes; • Include custom-designed carriers and fixtures configured for NRC-CPFC applications; • Allow devices to remain mounted in the same carrier throughout burn-in and characterization activities without removal, remounting, repositioning, or re-alignment; • Maintain consistent mechanical, electrical, thermal, and optical interfaces during transfer between processes; • Include integrated software capable of managing device identification, test sequencing, automated data collection, and data traceability across both subsystems; • Be supplied as a commercially available solution from a single manufacturer responsible for overall hardware, firmware, software, carrier architecture, and system integration. Solutions requiring separate software environments, third-party integration, separate carriers, adapters, or manual device transfer will not be considered compliant. • The integrated software must support device identification and test history across subsystems and export data in open formats (e.g., CSV or equivalent). B. Burn-In Subsystem Requirements The burn-in subsystem must provide: • A minimum of two (2) integrated burn-in racks; • A minimum of fourteen (14) burn-in drawers; • A minimum of fifty-six (56) burn-in fixtures; • A minimum of fifty-six (56) compatible device carriers; • A minimum of 384 independent source-measure channels; • Automatic Current Control (ACC) and Automatic Power Control (APC) operating modes; • Current drive capability of at least 500 mA per channel; • Compliance voltage of at least 7 V; • Temperature-controlled burn-in operation from approximately 45°C to at least 125°C; • Integrated LIV measurement capability; • In-situ electrical and optical monitoring during burn-in testing; • Electrostatic discharge protection for devices under test. The software must support monitoring and trending of: • Threshold current; • Slope efficiency; • Series resistance; and • Turn-on voltage throughout burn-in and ageing testing. C. Characterization Subsystem Requirements The characterization subsystem must provide: • One (1) automated laser diode characterization system; • One (1) tri-temperature control subsystem capable of sub-ambient operation; • Four (4) compatible characterization carriers; • Automated LIV characterization capability; • Optical spectrum analysis capability; • Automated optical alignment capability; • Fibre-coupled testing capability; • Automated test execution and data storage functionality. The subsystem must support: • Current ranges from approximately 10 mA to 1000 mA; • Optical power measurements from approximately 1 mW to at least 400 mW; • Wavelength measurements from approximately 900 nm to 1700 nm; • Spectral resolution of 0.02 nm or better; • Temperature control from approximately -5°C to 85°C; • Dry gas purge capability. D. Engineering, Installation, Training, Support and Electrical Compliance The supplier must provide: • Engineering and customization services necessary to configure the System for NRC-CPFC devices; • Factory verification and associated documentation; • Provision of current calibration certificates for measurement instruments used during acceptance testing; • Shipping preparation, crating, vacuum sealing, and handling services; • Delivery to NRC-CPFC in Ottawa, Ontario; • Installation and commissioning of the complete System; • On-site training for up to five (5) NRC personnel; • Completion of a Site Acceptance Test or equivalent acceptance process - At least ten (10) business days prior to SAT, the supplier must submit a SAT Plan for NRC approval, including test cases and procedures, configurations/fixtures, identified test equipment and calibration status, acceptance criteria and tolerances, sample sizes, and data capture templates/file formats; • A minimum twelve (12) month warranty; • Technical support services and availability of critical spare parts. The proposed System must be designed and manufactured to support field evaluation and site certification in accordance with the Canadian Electrical Code, Part I. title: X-ray Diffraction System (XRD)
description: This Contract will procure and install a high-resolution X-ray diffractometry (HR-XRD) system for use in the Epitaxy facilities at the National Research Council Canada (NRC). This HR-XRD system will provide critical feedback for the growth of III-V semiconductor heterostructures grown epitaxially. These systems are used for research and commercial growth of III-V semiconductors (arsenides, antimonides, and phosphides). These systems grow demanding heterostructures for a wide range of optoelectronic and quantum applications, such as: quantum dot lasers, InP-based nanowire quantum dots for single-photon emission, quantum cascade and interband cascade lasers, and GaSb-based diode lasers incorporating quaternary and quinary alloys.

title: Turbine-powered long-range beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS)-ready vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) Remotely Pilot Aerial Systems (RPAS)
description: The National Research Council of Canada's (NRC) Centre for Drone Innovation, part of the Drone and Flight Autonomy Laboratory, has a requirement for the supply of one (1) turbinepowered, long-range, heavy-payload, beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS)-ready vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) remotely piloted aircraft system (RPAS), the SwissDrones SDO 50 V3, including one (1) ground control station and a multi-link communications system. The system will provide a runway-independent aerial research platform for the integration and deployment of specialized scientific remote-sensing payloads in remote, infrastructure-limited and operationally demanding environments. The requirement includes original equipment manufacturer (OEM) integration of NRC's scientific sensors — one (1) HySpex Mjolnir VS620 hyperspectral imaging system and one (1) RIEGL VQ-840-GE LiDAR system — as well as manufacturer-provided pilot and maintenance training, an initial maintenance support package, spare assemblies, ground support equipment and technical support, with a minimum twelve (12) month warranty. Delivery of the complete system is required to NRC, Ottawa, Ontario, no later than March 31, 2027.

title: Consolidation of the Côte Dinan rock face – Quebec Field Unit
description: 5P468-26-0146/A Consolidation of the Côte Dinan rock face – Quebec Field Unit BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA, YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to the bid solicitation is soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca . Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. REQUIREMENT Parks Canada, owner of lot 1,212,705, wishes to carry out rock face stabilization works on Côte Dinan between Côte du Palais and Côte de la Canoterie. To assist with bonding and insurance requirements, this project is estimated at a value between $250,001 > $ 500,000, Taxes extra. TWO-SUBMISSION BID This Bid shall be submitted following a “two-submission” procedure. Refer to SI04 of the Special Instructions to Bidders. CONTRACTOR SELECTION AND OPTIONAL INDIGENOUS PARTICIPATION PLAN The Contractor should ensure provision of specific and agreed upon benefits for Indigenous People and Indigenous Businesses in the Area of the Contract. This Invitation to Tender contains bid criteria in order to provide socioeconomic benefits to Indigenous communities within the area covered by the contract. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE Contractor must perform and complete the Work no later than December 31, 2026.. OPTIONAL SITE VISIT It is recommended that the Bidder or a representative of the Bidder visit the work site. Arrangements have been made for the site visit to be held on the boardwalk in front of 11 Côte Dinan, Québec, QC G1K 8N6, on August 19, 2026. The site visit will begin at 9:30 AM EDT. Bidders must communicate with the Contracting Authority no later than 24h before the optional site visit to confirm attendance and provide the name(s) of the person(s) who will attend. Bidders will be requested to sign an attendance sheet. No alternative appointment will be given to bidders who do not attend or do not send a representative. Bidders who do not participate in the visit will not be precluded from submitting a bid. Any clarifications or changes to the bid solicitation resulting from the site visit will be included as an amendment to the bid solicitation. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than five (5) business days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

title: Submarine Force Museum Museum Display Cases
description: The purpose of amendment 0001 on 9/3 is to add the PDF copy of the SOW that includes the photos. The Submarine Force Museum (SFM) intends to procure two (2) conservation-grade (i.e. made from archival materials that are inert and will not off-gas or cause damage to the artifacts) microclimate museum display cases for use in future exhibits. This is part of a broader strategy to update all cases in the museum to have a uniform appearance and to meet museum preservation standards. These cases will help SFM meet current preservation standards while displaying artifacts from its historic collections, as the current cases which can accommodate mannequins do not meet museum preservation standards and are causing degradation to the artifacts on display. These cases will increase flexibility and mobility when creating new exhibits, as they are moveable, unlike the current cases. Conservation-grade cases will also allow SFM to borrow artifacts from other institutions which require more stringent display preservation standards than the current cases allow. These new cases will replace a double mannequin case that was previously loaned to SFM but is now being recalled. These cases will allow SFM to continue displaying the two mannequins assigned to this exhibit, thus preventing disruption of display and the visitor experience. These new cases should align with the design, engineering, and appearance of the ones already installed in the exhibit (see reference photos below; these cases were the first to be designed and engineered as part of the case updating strategy and therefore, they form the benchmark by which all other cases will be created), with any desired differences and exceptions noted here. Please see attached solicitation for full details.

description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT, NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. A REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) WILL NOT BE ISSUED AND QUOTES WILL NOT BE REQUESTED. The National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS) Rare Diseases Clinical Research Network (RDCRN) intends to award a firm fixed price sole source contract under the authority of FAR 12.102(a), only one source being available to meet the Government's needs, to: Carahsoft Technology Corp 11493 Sunset Hills Road Suite 100 Reston, VA 20190 NCATS hereby submits a notice of intent to award a sole source firm fixed price purchase order for the renewal of the existing Pantheon Platform Licenses and Support which includes associated maintenance, upgrades, and technical support, for a twelve (12) month period of performance commencing within thirty (30) days of award. Pantheon is required as the specified brand name because the RDCRN consortia websites and the network site (www.rarediseasenetwork.org) were built on and are currently hosted within the Pantheon platform, and the renewal continues an established production environment whose configuration, versioning history, automated backups, and Drupal upgrade cadence are natively integrated into Pantheon's proprietary infrastructure. This is not a new requirement. Although this contract is now expired, the requirement remains current and ongoing. Continued access to the platform is necessary to avoid interruption to established scientific and informatics workflows that support NCATS research. title: Ultra-High Vacuum (UHV) Translation Stages
description: Background The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is embarking on a project to support the Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography (EUVL) community by developing characterization of EUV scintillator materials. Many techniques for measuring spatial distribution (or image) of EUV rely on scintillators or devices that convert EUV radiation into visible light. Scintillators tend to be robust and afford the user the ability to use less costly and easier to characterize, visible light detection or imaging systems. However, their characterization requires specialized techniques and hardware which NIST must develop in order to provide accurate characterization of the performance of EUV scintillators. This requirement supports the �Optical Metrology for EUV Generation� Project under Grand Challenge 2, �Advanced Metrology for Future Microelectronics Manufacturing,� for CHIPS R&D Metrology. This requirement enables NIST to construct an ultra-high vacuum microscope to operate in NIST Synchrotron Ultraviolet Research Facility (SURF III) EUV reflectometer beamline. The microscope will allow for the measurement of EUV scintillator efficiency, output spectrum and point spread function. Minimum Capabilities that NIST Requires and for Which Information is Being Requested DRAFT MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS Description: UHV translation stages Quantity: 10 Technical Specifications Ultra-high vacuum compatible: low-outgassing materials, pressure range 10-8 Torr or better: Polyimide or PTFE insulated wire cables with braided, silver-plated copper shielding. All Stainless steel (18-8 or similar) hardware and plain finish materials (no anodization or paint). Stainless steel bearings lubricated with UHV-compatible lubricants (10-9 Torr or better rated at room temperature, no silicone-based lubricants) Vented holes or vented hardware used in unvented blind holes. Minimum bake out temperature 100�C. Travel Range: 50 mm minimum, 55 mm maximum Crossed roller bearing travel with piezo-electric actuator Compact size: < 20 mm thick, 85 mm long, 50 mm wide Closed loop operation: encoder resolution < 10 �m In vacuum cable length: 2 m (minimum) Vacuum interface cabling must use 15-pin D-sub connection and include connectors (PEEK material on vacuum side) Load capacity: 1 kg or more Stages must be cleaned for UHV compatibility, packaged and sealed to maintain cleanliness and be ready for 10-8 Torr base pressure operation with minimal cleaning (alcohol wipe). Description: Motion controller/amplifier Quantity: 10 Technical Specifications 2 units (5 axes each) to control all combined stages in line item 1 Include power supply for each unit: Electrical Requirements: Input Voltage: 120 VAC�10% (108--132 VAC) Frequency: 60 Hz�3 Hz Power Cord: Detachable 6+ ft line cord, IEC C13 to NEMA 5-15P plug Compliance: UL 62368-1 (or relevant IEEE/ANSI standard), FCC Part 15 Class A/B Controller to motor connector cable length: 2 m minimum Ethernet communication LabView programming library Include all power, motor and communication cables. Vacuum interface cabling must use 15-pin D-sub connection and include connectors. Include all required adapters to operate stages in air (w/o feedthrough flange). Description: 6� CFF electrical feed through flanges Quantity: 2 Technical Specifications Feedthrough flanges to support 8 axes per flange motor control operation in atmosphere and motor actuation in vacuum 6� CFF (DN100CF) knife edge flange platform, non-rotatable, clearance holes for sealing fasteners. UHV vacuum rated: pressure range 10-8 Torr or better. Quantity 2, 6� CFF with qty. 8, 15 pin D-dub feed throughs on each flange. title: Virtual Industry Day for FY27 USACE National Dredging Procurement Strategies
description: The Virtual Industry Day Meeting for the USACE National Dredging Center will occur on 09 Sept 2026 at 13:00 PM EST via Teams. All interested dredging companies are encouraged to attend. During the meeting, we will be discussing three potential planned national contract acquisition strategies. 1. Hopper Contracts: The National Dredging Center anticipates awarding multiple maintenance dredging and beach renourishment projects as consolidated contracts. See the attached spreadsheet Attachment 2 for proposed pairings for consolidated procurement packages. We anticipate the pairings of the attached projects and encourage feedback from industry on any of our projected pairings. 2. Scope Dredge to Budget: Optimize the Budget in terms of quality, scope, durability with innovative betterments and betterments within the budget. The goal of the scope-dredge to budget is maximizing achievable scope within a target budget that will be provided in the solicitation. The National Dredging Team intends to issue 1 solicitation for the Galveston/Houston Area of Responsibility. Phase One -A technical qualifications-based evaluation of initial proposals -RFP that defines the project with functional and performance requirements, budget cap, and schedule/delivery requirements -A statement of the maximum number of offerors that will be selected to submit Phase 2 proposals. -RFO FAR 36.101-2(b)(4) states maximum number of offerors shall not exceed five (5) Phase One proposals from vendors do not include: -Detailed design information -Cost or price information Down-select Decision for most highly qualified offerors in accordance with the solicitation. Proposed Phase 1 Qualifications -Proof of bonding capacity -Past Performance -Proposed Plant Proprietary Meetings (RFO FAR 15.101 Exchanges with Industry before receipt of proposals) Phase Two in accordance with FAR 15 Source Selection Procedures to determine best value. Official Phase Two RFP issued by amendment for most highly qualified offerors to submit phase-two competitive proposals that include technical proposals and cost or price information. Proposed Phase 2 Evaluation Factors -Maximum amount of time to maintain the channels at authorized dimensions -Maximum use of beneficial use -Schedule -Management Approach The harbors to be dredged include the Sabine-Neches Waterway, Galveston Harbor & Channel, Houston Ship Channel, Texas City Ship Channel, Freeport Harbor, Matagorda Ship Channel, Corpus Christi Ship Channel, Brazos Island Harbor, Gulf Intracoastal Waterway & Tributaries, Channel to Victoria, and Channel to Harlington. See Attachment 1 for project descriptions and map. 3. National Small Business Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC): The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) executes construction contracts for regular, reoccurring, and emergency National Enterprise Dredging requirements at various coastal harbors, inland rivers, canals, and connecting channels throughout the United States. Individual projects are typically annual requirements and may utilize mechanical, hydraulic, or a combination of dredging equipment and techniques with activities to include but not limited to maintenance and new work dredging, dredged material placement, and other activities such as Confined Disposal Facility (CDF), Dredged Material Disposal Facility (DMDF), or upland containment facility maintenance, groundskeeping, other earthwork at placement sites, surveying, or other work connected with dredging and placement requirements. Task orders issued under this MATOC will require the contractor to mobilize dredge plant and support vessels to the project location, perform dredging as shown on the respective plan(s), place dredged material�which may include beach nourishment, open-water placement, CDFs, DMDFs, beneficial use, or alternative placement strategies as indicated in individual task orders�and demobilize once complete. The maximum ordering capacity for the 5-year ordering period of the MATOC and maximum task order amounts are TBD. Below are the draft source selection criteria proposed: FACTOR 1: Technical Capability Submission Requirements: Dredge Information: The offeror shall provide documentation for any dredges being proposed for use under this solicitation/contract, and any subsequent task orders. If the proposal does not include at least one of the identified dredges below, then Factor 1 will be rated �Unacceptable�. Proposed dredges must include a minimum of at least one of the following: Cutter Suction Dredge - employs a mechanical cutter to break up material which is then excavated hydraulically and transported to the placement site through a pipeline. Minimum Requirement: 10-inch discharge diameter or larger Mechanical Dredge - uses of some form of bucket to excavate and raise submerged material. Minimum Requirement: 5 cubic yard bucket or larger Offeror can submit more than one dredge(s) that meets the minimum requirements above in responding to this evaluation factor. Dredges that are still under construction or are in the process of undergoing major reconstruction will not be considered. The dredge documentation must include the following information: dredge type; certify that the dredge meets minimum requirements stated above; proof offeror owns the dredges submitted (leased dredges are not acceptable). FACTOR 2: Past Performance Submission Requirements: Offerors will be required to provide three (3) past performance examples of recent and relevant maintenance dredging projects for the type of dredge submitted under Factor 1 � Technical Capability, which demonstrate that they have experience accomplishing the following: dredging of Navigation Channels, Rivers, Harbors, Inland Waterways with depths ranging from 6 feet to 50 feet. The past performance examples must include dredging that has been performed within the last six (6) years from the date of the solicitation. In addition to submitted examples, the Government may review any other sources of information for evaluation of past performance. If the Offeror is proposing as a Joint Venture (JV), Partnership and/or Teaming Arrangement and past performance cannot be provided as such, each partner shall submit past performance information but shall not exceed the three (3) projects total for this factor. 1. Note 1: NAA: The Offeror will be required to provide documentation related to EM 385-1-1 requirements such as Floating Service Naval Architecture Analysis (NAA) with either MATOC or Task Order proposal. 2. Note 2: The Offeror may be required to submit a letter of commitment with their proposal from a surety that confirms that the offeror's bonding capacity meets a specified minimum amount. Please RSVP no later than 10AM ET 08 September 2026 to both Ros Shoemaker and Terri Adams at Rosalind.m.shoemaker@usace.army.mil and terri.m.adamsl@usace.army.mil if you plan to attend the Industry Day. A Teams calendar invite will be sent out to all RSVP�s. Industry is also encouraged to provide any feedback on the proposed acquisition strategies or contract pairings. Feedback can be provided via email to the contracting officer and contract specialist listed above. If you would like to provide any questions in advance of the meeting, please provide them no later than 10AM ET, 08 September 2026.

title: Virtual Industry Day for FY27 USACE National Dredging Procurement Strategies
description: The Virtual Industry Day Meeting for the USACE National Dredging Center will occur on 09 Sept 2026 at 13:00 PM EST via Teams. All interested dredging companies are encouraged to attend. During the meeting, we will be discussing three potential planned national contract acquisition strategies. 1. Hopper Contracts: The National Dredging Center anticipates awarding multiple maintenance dredging and beach renourishment projects as consolidated contracts. See the attached spreadsheet Attachment 2 for proposed pairings for consolidated procurement packages. We anticipate the pairings of the attached projects and encourage feedback from industry on any of our projected pairings. 2. Scope Dredge to Budget: Optimize the Budget in terms of quality, scope, durability with innovative betterments and betterments within the budget. The goal of the scope-dredge to budget is maximizing achievable scope within a target budget that will be provided in the solicitation. The National Dredging Team intends to issue 1 solicitation for the Galveston/Houston Area of Responsibility. Phase One -A technical qualifications-based evaluation of initial proposals -RFP that defines the project with functional and performance requirements, budget cap, and schedule/delivery requirements -A statement of the maximum number of offerors that will be selected to submit Phase 2 proposals. -RFO FAR 36.101-2(b)(4) states maximum number of offerors shall not exceed five (5) Phase One proposals from vendors do not include: -Detailed design information -Cost or price information Down-select Decision for most highly qualified offerors in accordance with the solicitation. Proposed Phase 1 Qualifications -Proof of bonding capacity -Past Performance -Proposed Plant Proprietary Meetings (RFO FAR 15.101 Exchanges with Industry before receipt of proposals) Phase Two in accordance with FAR 15 Source Selection Procedures to determine best value. Official Phase Two RFP issued by amendment for most highly qualified offerors to submit phase-two competitive proposals that include technical proposals and cost or price information. Proposed Phase 2 Evaluation Factors -Maximum amount of time to maintain the channels at authorized dimensions -Maximum use of beneficial use -Schedule -Management Approach The harbors to be dredged include the Sabine-Neches Waterway, Galveston Harbor & Channel, Houston Ship Channel, Texas City Ship Channel, Freeport Harbor, Matagorda Ship Channel, Corpus Christi Ship Channel, Brazos Island Harbor, Gulf Intracoastal Waterway & Tributaries, Channel to Victoria, and Channel to Harlington. See Attachment 1 for project descriptions and map. 3. National Small Business Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC): The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) executes construction contracts for regular, reoccurring, and emergency National Enterprise Dredging requirements at various coastal harbors, inland rivers, canals, and connecting channels throughout the United States. Individual projects are typically annual requirements and may utilize mechanical, hydraulic, or a combination of dredging equipment and techniques with activities to include but not limited to maintenance and new work dredging, dredged material placement, and other activities such as Confined Disposal Facility (CDF), Dredged Material Disposal Facility (DMDF), or upland containment facility maintenance, groundskeeping, other earthwork at placement sites, surveying, or other work connected with dredging and placement requirements. Task orders issued under this MATOC will require the contractor to mobilize dredge plant and support vessels to the project location, perform dredging as shown on the respective plan(s), place dredged material�which may include beach nourishment, open-water placement, CDFs, DMDFs, beneficial use, or alternative placement strategies as indicated in individual task orders�and demobilize once complete. The maximum ordering capacity for the 5-year ordering period of the MATOC and maximum task order amounts are TBD. Below are the draft source selection criteria proposed: FACTOR 1: Technical Capability Submission Requirements: Dredge Information: The offeror shall provide documentation for any dredges being proposed for use under this solicitation/contract, and any subsequent task orders. If the proposal does not include at least one of the identified dredges below, then Factor 1 will be rated �Unacceptable�. Proposed dredges must include a minimum of at least one of the following: Cutter Suction Dredge - employs a mechanical cutter to break up material which is then excavated hydraulically and transported to the placement site through a pipeline. Minimum Requirement: 10-inch discharge diameter or larger Mechanical Dredge - uses of some form of bucket to excavate and raise submerged material. Minimum Requirement: 5 cubic yard bucket or larger Offeror can submit more than one dredge(s) that meets the minimum requirements above in responding to this evaluation factor. Dredges that are still under construction or are in the process of undergoing major reconstruction will not be considered. The dredge documentation must include the following information: dredge type; certify that the dredge meets minimum requirements stated above; proof offeror owns the dredges submitted (leased dredges are not acceptable). description: NON-COMPETITIVE COMBINED SYNOPSIS / SOLICITATION Title: L-Glutamic Acid (i) This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This solicitation is issued as a Notice of Intent (NOI) for a non-competitive combined synopsis/solicitation to award a contract or purchase order without providing for full and open competition (including brand-name, if applicable). This acquisition is conducted under the authority of FAR 12.603, Streamlined Solicitation for Commercial Products or Commercial Services, and is not expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold. Additional authority includes 41 U.S.C. 1901 and FAR 6.302-3(a)(2)(ii). The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of the Director, Office of Acquisitions, intends to negotiate and award a firm-fixed price on a non-competitive basis to Sigma-Aldrich Inc., 3050 Spruce St., Saint Louis, Missouri 63103 for the requested L-Glutamic Acid (2,4 ��C2-99%). (iii) The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 dated March 13, 2026. (iv) The associated NAICS code is 325180 � Other Basic Inorganic Chemical Manufacturing, and the small business size standard is 1,000 in number of employees. This requirement is not a set-aside for small business. (v) Description of Requirement: This requirement is to obtain a special Sigma-Aldrich Inc., 13C2 L-Glutamic Acid 2,4 99%,1x1 gram. The Magnetic Resonance (MR) Spectroscopy Unit and Core have been conducting several in vivo carbon-13 (1*3C) spectroscopy projects with infusion of 13C labeled chemicals. Because natural abundance of 1*3C is only 1% and is too weak to be detected. Therefore, we need to use chemicals with enriched 13C to increase 13C signal intensity. With these 13C labelled chemicals, we will be able to detect brain metabolism and to accurately measure the concentrations of several important metabolites. The 13C MR spectroscopy methods developed in our group is and will be applied to many other research groups in NIMH and NIH for various neural science studies. Without this chemical, the institute will lose a powerful method in neural science research. title: Virtual Industry Day for FY27 USACE National Dredging Procurement Strategies
description: The Virtual Industry Day Meeting for the USACE National Dredging Center will occur on 09 Sept 2026 at 13:00 PM EST via Teams. All interested dredging companies are encouraged to attend. During the meeting, we will be discussing three potential planned national contract acquisition strategies. 1. Hopper Contracts: The National Dredging Center anticipates awarding multiple maintenance dredging and beach renourishment projects as consolidated contracts. See the attached spreadsheet Attachment 2 for proposed pairings for consolidated procurement packages. We anticipate the pairings of the attached projects and encourage feedback from industry on any of our projected pairings. 2. Scope Dredge to Budget: Optimize the Budget in terms of quality, scope, durability with innovative betterments and betterments within the budget. The goal of the scope-dredge to budget is maximizing achievable scope within a target budget that will be provided in the solicitation. The National Dredging Team intends to issue 1 solicitation for the Galveston/Houston Area of Responsibility. Phase One -A technical qualifications-based evaluation of initial proposals -RFP that defines the project with functional and performance requirements, budget cap, and schedule/delivery requirements -A statement of the maximum number of offerors that will be selected to submit Phase 2 proposals. -RFO FAR 36.101-2(b)(4) states maximum number of offerors shall not exceed five (5) Phase One proposals from vendors do not include: -Detailed design information -Cost or price information Down-select Decision for most highly qualified offerors in accordance with the solicitation. Proposed Phase 1 Qualifications -Proof of bonding capacity -Past Performance -Proposed Plant Proprietary Meetings (RFO FAR 15.101 Exchanges with Industry before receipt of proposals) Phase Two in accordance with FAR 15 Source Selection Procedures to determine best value. Official Phase Two RFP issued by amendment for most highly qualified offerors to submit phase-two competitive proposals that include technical proposals and cost or price information. Proposed Phase 2 Evaluation Factors -Maximum amount of time to maintain the channels at authorized dimensions -Maximum use of beneficial use -Schedule -Management Approach The harbors to be dredged include the Sabine-Neches Waterway, Galveston Harbor & Channel, Houston Ship Channel, Texas City Ship Channel, Freeport Harbor, Matagorda Ship Channel, Corpus Christi Ship Channel, Brazos Island Harbor, Gulf Intracoastal Waterway & Tributaries, Channel to Victoria, and Channel to Harlington. See Attachment 1 for project descriptions and map. 3. National Small Business Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC): The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) executes construction contracts for regular, reoccurring, and emergency National Enterprise Dredging requirements at various coastal harbors, inland rivers, canals, and connecting channels throughout the United States. Individual projects are typically annual requirements and may utilize mechanical, hydraulic, or a combination of dredging equipment and techniques with activities to include but not limited to maintenance and new work dredging, dredged material placement, and other activities such as Confined Disposal Facility (CDF), Dredged Material Disposal Facility (DMDF), or upland containment facility maintenance, groundskeeping, other earthwork at placement sites, surveying, or other work connected with dredging and placement requirements. Task orders issued under this MATOC will require the contractor to mobilize dredge plant and support vessels to the project location, perform dredging as shown on the respective plan(s), place dredged material�which may include beach nourishment, open-water placement, CDFs, DMDFs, beneficial use, or alternative placement strategies as indicated in individual task orders�and demobilize once complete. The maximum ordering capacity for the 5-year ordering period of the MATOC and maximum task order amounts are TBD. Below are the draft source selection criteria proposed: FACTOR 1: Technical Capability Submission Requirements: Dredge Information: The offeror shall provide documentation for any dredges being proposed for use under this solicitation/contract, and any subsequent task orders. If the proposal does not include at least one of the identified dredges below, then Factor 1 will be rated �Unacceptable�. Proposed dredges must include a minimum of at least one of the following: Cutter Suction Dredge - employs a mechanical cutter to break up material which is then excavated hydraulically and transported to the placement site through a pipeline. Minimum Requirement: 10-inch discharge diameter or larger Mechanical Dredge - uses of some form of bucket to excavate and raise submerged material. Minimum Requirement: 5 cubic yard bucket or larger Offeror can submit more than one dredge(s) that meets the minimum requirements above in responding to this evaluation factor. Dredges that are still under construction or are in the process of undergoing major reconstruction will not be considered. The dredge documentation must include the following information: dredge type; certify that the dredge meets minimum requirements stated above; proof offeror owns the dredges submitted (leased dredges are not acceptable). FACTOR 2: Past Performance Submission Requirements: Offerors will be required to provide three (3) past performance examples of recent and relevant maintenance dredging projects for the type of dredge submitted under Factor 1 � Technical Capability, which demonstrate that they have experience accomplishing the following: dredging of Navigation Channels, Rivers, Harbors, Inland Waterways with depths ranging from 6 feet to 50 feet. The past performance examples must include dredging that has been performed within the last six (6) years from the date of the solicitation. In addition to submitted examples, the Government may review any other sources of information for evaluation of past performance. If the Offeror is proposing as a Joint Venture (JV), Partnership and/or Teaming Arrangement and past performance cannot be provided as such, each partner shall submit past performance information but shall not exceed the three (3) projects total for this factor. 1. Note 1: NAA: The Offeror will be required to provide documentation related to EM 385-1-1 requirements such as Floating Service Naval Architecture Analysis (NAA) with either MATOC or Task Order proposal. 2. Note 2: The Offeror may be required to submit a letter of commitment with their proposal from a surety that confirms that the offeror's bonding capacity meets a specified minimum amount. Please RSVP no later than 10AM ET 08 September 2026 to both Ros Shoemaker and Terri Adams at Rosalind.m.shoemaker@usace.army.mil and terri.m.adams@usace.army.mil if you plan to attend the Industry Day. A Teams calendar invite will be sent out to all RSVP�s. Industry is also encouraged to provide any feedback on the proposed acquisition strategies or contract pairings. Feedback can be provided via email to the contracting officer and contract specialist listed above. If you would like to provide any questions in advance of the meeting, please provide them no later than 10AM ET, 08 September 2026.

title: Submarine Force Museum Museum Display Cases
description: The Submarine Force Museum (SFM) intends to procure two (2) conservation-grade (i.e. made from archival materials that are inert and will not off-gas or cause damage to the artifacts) microclimate museum display cases for use in future exhibits. This is part of a broader strategy to update all cases in the museum to have a uniform appearance and to meet museum preservation standards. These cases will help SFM meet current preservation standards while displaying artifacts from its historic collections, as the current cases which can accommodate mannequins do not meet museum preservation standards and are causing degradation to the artifacts on display. These cases will increase flexibility and mobility when creating new exhibits, as they are moveable, unlike the current cases. Conservation-grade cases will also allow SFM to borrow artifacts from other institutions which require more stringent display preservation standards than the current cases allow. These new cases will replace a double mannequin case that was previously loaned to SFM but is now being recalled. These cases will allow SFM to continue displaying the two mannequins assigned to this exhibit, thus preventing disruption of display and the visitor experience. These new cases should align with the design, engineering, and appearance of the ones already installed in the exhibit (see reference photos below; these cases were the first to be designed and engineered as part of the case updating strategy and therefore, they form the benchmark by which all other cases will be created), with any desired differences and exceptions noted here. Please see attached solicitation for full details.

title: Z2NZ--659-24-203: Extend Chilled Water to Hospice and Audiology
description: Subject: Statement of Work: Install Chill Water Lines to Hospice and Audiology Location: Campus Project #: 659-24-203 Date: 26 February 2026 STATEMENT OF WORK Mechanical General: The project involves providing chilled Water from Building 31 primary chiller to serve Buildings 42 and 43. This project should be completed in 365 days and include a 1-year warranty on all items. Background Information: Building 42 and Building 43 are on separate systems, the VA wants them on the same system as Building 31. SCOPE OF WORK: Provide chilled water from the building 31 primary chiller to serve Buildings 42 and 43, bypassing the existing chillers in 42 and 43 during normal operation. Normal Operation (Primary from Building 31) Building 42 and Building 43 are served directly from building 31 chilled-water plant. The existing chillers for 42 and 43 are isolated and not in use. Valves and actuators shall be connected to the Building Management System (BMS) and automatically controlled for mode selection. Bypass Mode (Local Chillers in Service) Building 42: The existing chiller serves the 2" chilled-water line supplying Audiology. Glycol shall be replenished through the pot feeder. Building 43: The existing chiller serves the 3" chilled-water line supplying the building. Glycol shall be replenished through the pot feeder. New Work / Modifications Install additional pumps in Building 42 to serve the 2" chilled-water line to Audiology. Run new 4" chilled-water supply and return lines from Building 31 to Building 43. Provide emergency backup chilled-water access: Building 42: Quick-connect ports. Building 43: Bolted flange connection. All new valves and actuators shall be BMS-integrated for automatic operation and remote monitoring. Contractor Trades: Division 01 General Requirements Rig, hoist, and place pumps, long pipe runs, and large valves especially for elevated or exterior segments. Develop and execute functional performance tests for both modes, including BMS sequences, alarms, failover, and remote monitoring. Produce pre-functional checklists, FPT scripts, deficiency logs, and final Cx report. Implement Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) measures near Audiology and any patient-care areas: barriers, negative air, dust control, HEPA, clean paths. Noise/vibration management during coring and pump installation; off-hours work planning if needed. Maintain life safety (egress, fire alarm impairments) and hot work permits. Mechanical/Electrical permits, right-of-way if exterior work crosses public domain, and VA safety protocols. Badging and security clearances for contractors working on campus. Division 2: Existing Conditions Hazardous materials handling for penetrations in older construction (asbestos/lead). Perform pre-work survey and abate if found. Preconstruction survey of pipe routing; locates for existing utilities; as-builts for final turnover. Division 03 -Concrete Install housekeeping pads for pumps or associated equipment in Bldg. 42. Perform core drilling, sleeves, and wall/floor penetrations; patch and restore finishes. Division 23: HVAC Install new 4" chilled-water supply and return from Building 31 to Building 43 (routing, piping, valves, bolted flange connection at Bldg. 43). Add pumps in Building 42 to serve the 2" CHW line to Audiology (set pumps, suction/discharge fittings, check valves, balancing valves). Install quick-connect ports at Building 42 and bolted flange at Building 43 for emergency backup CHW access. Provide/replace valves and actuators; isolate existing chillers in 42 and 43 for normal operation; configure bypass tie-ins. Hot work (welding/brazing), threaded/flanged connections, equipment anchorage, and system rinsing/flush. Integrate valves and actuators into BMS for automatic mode selection (Normal vs. Bypass). Provide points list, sequences of operation, graphics, and alarm/notification setup. Program interlocks between Building 31 plant and local chillers; ensure remote monitoring visibility. Coordinate network connectivity to VA systems (per IT/security requirements). Insulate new and modified CHW piping, valves, and fittings; provide condensation control and energy code compliance. Apply pipe identification (color bands, flow arrows) and valve tags. Hydronic balancing of flows for both Normal Operation (from Bldg. 31) and Bypass Mode (local chillers). Verify T, pump head/curve alignment, and distribution performance to Audiology and Bldg. 43 loads. Provide glycol supply and concentration management (both buildings use pot feeders in Bypass Mode). Test inhibitor levels, pH, and conductivity; provide documentation and labels for glycol concentration. Touch-up coatings on exposed piping and supports; ASME A13.1 compliant pipe marking and valve tags. Division 26: Electrical Provide power to new pumps, actuators, and any control panels (breakers, disconnects, conduit, wiring). Install VFDs (if specified/required for pump control), control power transformers as needed. Bond/ground all new mechanical equipment and supports; label circuits. Division 27: Communications Run and terminate BMS cabling (twisted pair, network, I/O), install field panels, power supplies for actuators. Support the controls contractor with panel mounting, device terminations, and point-to-point checkout. Division 31 - Earthwork Trenching or directional boring, routing, backfill, and site restoration (hardscape/landscape). Coordinate utility locating (public + private locates) and storm/sanitary separation clearances. Division 32 Exterior Improvements Coordinate erosion & sediment control, site concrete/flatwork restoration: asphalt cut & patch; pavement markings. List of Deliverables: 1. Project Administration Deliverables Project Schedule (Preliminary + Baseline CPM) Phasing Plan (if applicable) Site Logistics / Staging Plan Contractor s Quality Control (CQC) Plan Accident Prevention Plan (APP) Activity Hazard Analyses (AHAs) Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA)/PCRA coordination documentation Emergency Response Plan Daily Reports 2. Submittals (01 33 23) Submittal Register (RFI/Submittal log) Product Data for all mechanical/electrical components Shop Drawings (piping layout, hangers, valves, insulation, electrical routing, controls) Samples (insulation, labeling, coatings if any) Certifications (welders, equipment, materials) O&M Manuals (Mechanical, Electrical, Controls) Training Materials (videos, agendas, attendance logs) 3. Safety Deliverables (01 35 26) Safety Orientation Documentation Hot Work Permits Fire Watch Logs Daily Safety Inspection Reports TB Testing Records (as required by VA) 4. Quality Control Deliverables (01 45 00) Preparatory Meeting Minutes Initial Phase Meeting Minutes Follow up QC Inspection Reports Testing Reports (pressure test, chemical cleaning, flushing, electrical testing, TAB reports) Deficiency/Punch list Logs 5. Environmental Controls Deliverables (01 57 19) Erosion and Sediment Control Plan Wastewater/Dewatering Plan Noise/Dust Control Measures 6. Waste Management Deliverables (01 74 19) Construction Waste Management Plan Waste Diversion Reports (monthly or final) 7. Division 23 Mechanical Deliverables Hydronic Piping Shop Drawings Valve & Equipment Schedules Pump Submittals (curves, motor data, VFD data) Insulation Submittals Water Treatment Plan & Reports Test, Flush, and Chemical Cleaning Reports TAB Report (Final) 8. Division 26 Electrical Deliverables Panel Schedules One Line Diagrams Conductor/Conduit Shop Drawings Grounding/Bonding Submittals Motor/Starter/VFD Submittals Electrical Testing Results (megger, torque logs, breaker verification) 9. Division 27 Communications / Controls Deliverables DDC Sequences of Operation DDC Shop Drawings & Network Architecture Controls Point to Point Checkout Sheets BACnet/IP Integration Documentation Graphics Screens (ECC) Controls Acceptance Test 10. Closeout Deliverables As Built Drawings (redlines + final CAD/PDF) Final O&M Manuals (Mechanical, Electrical, Controls) Warr

Normal Operation (Primary from Building 31) Building 42 and Building 43 are served directly from building 31 chilled-water plant. The existing chillers for 42 and 43 are isolated and not in use. Valves and actuators shall be connected to the Building Management System (BMS) and automatically controlled for mode selection. Bypass Mode (Local Chillers in Service) Building 42: The existing chiller serves the 2" chilled-water line supplying Audiology. Glycol shall be replenished through the pot feeder. Building 43: The existing chiller serves the 3" chilled-water line supplying the building. Glycol shall be replenished through the pot feeder. New Work / Modifications Install additional pumps in Building 42 to serve the 2" chilled-water line to Audiology. Run new 4" chilled-water supply and return lines from Building 31 to Building 43. Provide emergency backup chilled-water access: Building 42: Quick-connect ports. Building 43: Bolted flange connection. All new valves and actuators shall be BMS-integrated for automatic operation and remote monitoring. Contractor Trades: Division 01 General Requirements Rig, hoist, and place pumps, long pipe runs, and large valves especially for elevated or exterior segments. Develop and execute functional performance tests for both modes, including BMS sequences, alarms, failover, and remote monitoring. Produce pre-functional checklists, FPT scripts, deficiency logs, and final Cx report. Implement Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) measures near Audiology and any patient-care areas: barriers, negative air, dust control, HEPA, clean paths. Noise/vibration management during coring and pump installation; off-hours work planning if needed. Maintain life safety (egress, fire alarm impairments) and hot work permits. Mechanical/Electrical permits, right-of-way if exterior work crosses public domain, and VA safety protocols. Badging and security clearances for contractors working on campus. Division 2: Existing Conditions Hazardous materials handling for penetrations in older construction (asbestos/lead). Perform pre-work survey and abate if found. Preconstruction survey of pipe routing; locates for existing utilities; as-builts for final turnover. Division 03 -Concrete Install housekeeping pads for pumps or associated equipment in Bldg. 42. Perform core drilling, sleeves, and wall/floor penetrations; patch and restore finishes. Division 23: HVAC Install new 4" chilled-water supply and return from Building 31 to Building 43 (routing, piping, valves, bolted flange connection at Bldg. 43). Add pumps in Building 42 to serve the 2" CHW line to Audiology (set pumps, suction/discharge fittings, check valves, balancing valves). Install quick-connect ports at Building 42 and bolted flange at Building 43 for emergency backup CHW access. Provide/replace valves and actuators; isolate existing chillers in 42 and 43 for normal operation; configure bypass tie-ins. Hot work (welding/brazing), threaded/flanged connections, equipment anchorage, and system rinsing/flush. Integrate valves and actuators into BMS for automatic mode selection (Normal vs. Bypass). Provide points list, sequences of operation, graphics, and alarm/notification setup. Program interlocks between Building 31 plant and local chillers; ensure remote monitoring visibility. Coordinate network connectivity to VA systems (per IT/security requirements). Insulate new and modified CHW piping, valves, and fittings; provide condensation control and energy code compliance. Apply pipe identification (color bands, flow arrows) and valve tags. Hydronic balancing of flows for both Normal Operation (from Bldg. 31) and Bypass Mode (local chillers). Verify T, pump head/curve alignment, and distribution performance to Audiology and Bldg. 43 loads. Provide glycol supply and concentration management (both buildings use pot feeders in Bypass Mode). Test inhibitor levels, pH, and conductivity; provide documentation and labels for glycol concentration. Touch-up coatings on exposed piping and supports; ASME A13.1 compliant pipe marking and valve tags. Division 26: Electrical Provide power to new pumps, actuators, and any control panels (breakers, disconnects, conduit, wiring). Install VFDs (if specified/required for pump control), control power transformers as needed. Bond/ground all new mechanical equipment and supports; label circuits. Division 27: Communications Run and terminate BMS cabling (twisted pair, network, I/O), install field panels, power supplies for actuators. Support the controls contractor with panel mounting, device terminations, and point-to-point checkout. Division 31 - Earthwork Trenching or directional boring, routing, backfill, and site restoration (hardscape/landscape). Coordinate utility locating (public + private locates) and storm/sanitary separation clearances. Division 32 Exterior Improvements Coordinate erosion & sediment control, site concrete/flatwork restoration: asphalt cut & patch; pavement markings. List of Deliverables: 1. title: Acquisition of a Laboratory Microtome
description: The purpose of this project is to acquire one laboratory microtome for preparation of thin, reproducible tissue sections from paraffin-embedded specimens used in the Bladder Cancer Section's research. The microtome will support histologic evaluation, immunohistochemistry, and other tissue-based analyses needed to study mechanisms of resistance to antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) in bladder tumors. A dedicated microtome is justified to enable timely, consistent in-house sectioning of valuable research specimens, reduce dependence on shared equipment or external sectioning, and improve experimental reproducibility and workflow efficiency. The microtome must provide precise and reproducible section thickness control suitable for routine histology and research applications using paraffin-embedded tissue. The unit should provide stable specimen orientation and controlled sectioning, a secure blade holder with appropriate safety features, and an ergonomic design suitable for repeated laboratory use. Reliable mechanical performance is essential to produce intact, uniform tissue sections for downstream staining, imaging, and quantitative analysis.

title: Ultra-Low Temperature Upright Freezers
description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Requirement This Notice of Intent to Sole Source is not a solicitation. This is not a request for quotes. The Department of Veterans Affairs intends to negotiate a sole source contract with LabRepCo. Description: The Department of Veterans Affairs intends to negotiate a sole source contract with LabRepCo to procure two TwinGuard Ultra-Low Temperature Upright Freezers, model MDF-DU703VXHA-PA, for storing pre-clinical and clinical research samples at the White River Junction VA Healthcare System. The freezers are required to support research involving irreplaceable biofluid samples, including blood and saliva obtained from Veterans. The TwinGuard system provides two independent auto-cascade cooling systems that operate independently and concurrently to maintain temperature stability and protect samples in the event of a cooling-system failure. The system also provides insulated inner doors, a running temperature log, predictive analytics, and audible and visible alarms. Market research determined that no other freezer brands currently offer the required dual independent cooling-system and unique capability to fulfill the requirement. These unique characteristics are necessary to maintain the integrity and temperature stability of irreplaceable research samples. Therefore, it is the Government's belief that no other source can provide equipment that meets the required salient characteristics. Since the intent is to procure this requirement on a sole source basis, this notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. It is not a solicitation or request for offers and no solicitation will be posted to Contracting Opportunities on SAM.gov. The authority for this action is FAR 13.106-1(b), Soliciting from a Single Source. The NAICS is 333415. The size standard is 1,250 employees. The PSC/FSC is 4110. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government. Responses must be received no later than Tuesday, September 8, 2026, 10:00AM EST. No telephonic inquiries will be accepted. title: Netherlands – Measuring instruments – Seismological Instruments Lot 1 Surface Accelerometer en Lot 2 Dataloggers
description: The Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute (KNMI) is legally mandated to monitor and analyse seismic activity in and around the Netherlands. To fulfil this statutory responsibility, KNMI operates and maintains a nationwide seismic monitoring network consisting of multiple monitoring locations. Each location is equipped with seismological instruments and a data logger that records the measurement data and transmits it to KNMI's servers via a router. KNMI analyses these data to fulfil its legal mandate, and the data are also made publicly available for (scientific) research purposes. To maintain the monitoring network, KNMI requires seismological instruments that perform accurate and consistent seismic measurements and are capable of transmitting data to KNMI. As a contracting authority subject to public procurement legislation, KNMI is required to conduct procurement procedures for the acquisition of these instruments. The estimated magnitude for this requirement is between $100,000 and $250,000. description: W912EE - The United States Army Corps of Engineers, Vicksburg District, has issued an Invitation for Bids (IFB) Solicitation Number W912EE26BA007 for Tate County, MS, MDHP, LD-23-02, FC/MRT, Yazoo River Basin, Hickahala Senatobia Watershed. The work consists of furnishing all plant, labor, materials, and equipment, and constructing 5 low drop grade control structures in Tate County, Mississippi. Bids will be evaluated based on lowest price submitted. The magnitude of this construction project is estimated to be between $1 Million and $5 Million. title: INL Kyiv Ammunition
description: Update 9/3/2026 to post Question & Answer Responses document. The Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs (INL) supports partner nation police units. This acquisition will help equip specific units with ammunition required to defend themselves and carry out law enforcement duties. The requested ammunition will be used by Law Enforcement personnel during life threatening deadly force encounters and therefore reliability, durability, accuracy and proper function are paramount. The ammunition must be compatible and interoperable with U.S. provided weapons that include M4 Patrol rifles and duty handguns in service. SUBSTANTIVE REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall fulfill the following substantive requirements (See Attachment A RFQ/SOW for a complete listing of requirements): Please reference Item Specification details in Attachment. -5.56mm 62gr M855 20rnd Carton / Mil Spec & Mil Pack - Marking Green Tip, DODIC A059 10 round clip, military packaging or equal � Qty 3,000,000 rounds -9mm 124 GR FMJ M882 DODIC A363: Military packaging, can in crate � Qty 1,000,000 rounds -M855 62 gr Linked ammunition, NO TRACERS. DODIC A062 � Qty 2,500,000 rounds New product only. The offeror is responsible for obtaining all ammunition requested directly from the manufacturer, with no aftermarket parts/non-manufacturer parts incorporated in the weapons offered, 100% manufacturer assembly of all parts/components/equipment. The offeror is fully responsible for the delivery of safe, fully operational and complete ammunition. Ammunition shall be manufactured to/comply with US Military specifications DODICs and manufacturer will supply certification of testing to support quality assurance plan and applicable ISO 9001:2008 certification. Delivery All items shall be picked up from vendor location by State Department Freight Forwarder, DFS. Freight Forwarder Information and POC will follow after award and coordinated by the COR. Delivery shall be made FOB Origin as soon as possible but not later than 270 days from the date of contract award and in accordance with the instructions from the COR, post award. Submission Requirements (please see details in the Attachment A � RFQ/SOW) Evaluation Criteria (please see details in the Attachment A � RFQ/SOW) After initial evaluation of quotes, the Contracting Officer may negotiate final terms with one or more contractors of the Government�s choice before issuing a purchase order. The Contracting Officer will not negotiate with any contractors other than those of the Government�s choice and will not use the formal source selection procedures described in FAR Part 15. The Government may perform a comparative evaluation to select the contractor that provides the best value, considering the evaluation factors below. The Contracting Officer may issue a purchase order to other than the contractor with the lowest proposed price. The Government will consider the following factors when selecting contractors for award. The following factors shall be used to evaluate quotes: 1) Technical Specifications: Proposal must meet or exceed required technical specifications. Compliance with all technical specifications - Quality control documentation (ISO 9001:2008) 2) Delivery Timeline. 3) Export Compliance Experience: The entity demonstrating export compliance experience specific to weapons. 4) Past Performance: INL/Kyiv values direct past performance in weapons which demonstrates export compliance expertise and with deliveries to Ukraine. 5) Price: The overall price will be considered, and the lowest prices is favorable.
